chapters.title: The Doctor's Opinion
chapters.content: WE of Alcoholics Anonymous believe that the reader will be interested in the medical estimate of the plan of recovery described in this book. Convinced medical men realize that faith, and spiritual life, are the greatest bulwarks against all foes, and they have proved conclusively that of all diseases the most baffling is that of alcoholism. In the following chapter, there is a medical statement which may be regarded as an introduction to this book.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Bill's Story
chapters.content: WAR FEVER ran high in the New England town to which we new, young officers from Plattsburg were assigned, and we were flattered. Our social life was a dizzy round of receptions, dinners, and dances. The most coveted invitation was to the home of a lovely girl, who was soon to become my wife. How well I remember just before the wedding how concerned I was that my drinking should not interfere with the ceremony. I had a few drinks before the reception, none at the dinner, and none at the reception. I was very proud of my self-control, and fully convinced I could stop any time I wanted to.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: How It Works
chapters.content: RARELY HAVE we seen a person fail who has thoroughly followed our path. Those who do not recover are people who cannot or will not completely give themselves to this simple program, usually men and women who are constitutionally incapable of being honest with themselves. There are such unfortunates. They are not at fault; they seem to have been born that way. They are too ill to recover permanently. There are those, too, who suffer from grave emotional and mental disorders, but many of them do recover if they have the capacity to be honest.
